rule: Free function: its name (with the language's module qualifier where it has one). ... Kotlin top-level functions `com.x.f`.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type or object name) is method; a class-name call `T(..)` that resolves to a constructor, and `: this(..)` / `: super(..)` / a supertype-list call, are constructor. Kotlin has no `new`; a `val x = T(..)` constructor call is treated as decision A's `= new T(...)`. Top-level functions are package-qualified (`com.acme.calc.square`), with no file-facade class (`CalcKt`) in the ID. Report has no written constructor; `Report()` is high because the class is in the scan (SPEC's Java enum rule is high 'when the enum is in the scan' without a written constructor). `x * x` and `+` are arithmetic, not calls.
